title: SchemeTorsorPullbackEquivariantHomIsIso
statement: Let $i:Y_0\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $M$ a finite abelian group, and $t$ a scheme $M$-torsor over $Y$ [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor]. Set $G=\underline M_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $R$ be any $i^{-1}G$-torsor [def-sc-gm-torsor, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $f:i^{-1}_{\rm set}(t.\mathrm{sheaf})\to R.\mathrm{sheaf}$ any morphism of sheaves of sets. Suppose $f(\eta_T(g+\!_v x))=\eta_G(g)+\!_v f(\eta_T(x))$ over $W\times_Y Y_0$ for every $W\in Y_{\acute et}$, $g\in G(W)$ and $x\in t.\mathrm{sheaf}(W)$. Then $f$ is an isomorphism. This statement does not construct $f$, and assumes no scheme representative for $R$.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (2), (4); Tag 0A5G; Cohomology on Sites Section 03AG

proof.text: Use the unit-compatible comparison between abelian and set inverse image and preservation of finite limits to transport the torsor action and its simply transitive action isomorphism. The set inverse image is also a left adjoint, so it preserves epimorphisms and local nonemptiness. This gives a torsor structure on the source sheaf for the specified coefficient sheaf.

The inverse-image presheaf is a filtered colimit of sections over source-site objects followed by sheafification. Represent a coefficient and torsor section locally, refining to a common source object; unit equivariance gives equivariance there. Naturality and separatedness give full equivariance.

Locally trivialize the source torsor using local nonemptiness. An equivariant morphism between simply transitive group actions is bijective: translating a chosen source section identifies the map with the identity on the coefficient group. Thus f is locally bijective, hence an isomorphism of sheaves (equivalently use Torsor.Iso.ofHom).
